title: Spot Assay for Phage Plaque Counting
author: Marijn Ceelen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7i9hkh6

steps.title: Prepare E. coli Culture
steps.instruction: Prepare a susceptible E. coli strain (e.g., LE392 or DH10B) for the assay.

substeps.instruction: Streak E. coli on an LB plate and incubate overnight at 37 °C.
Pick a single colony and inoculate 10 mL of LB.
Incubate the culture at 37 °C until the OD reaches 2-3 (overnight culture recommended).

steps.title: Prepare Agar and Plates
steps.instruction: Prepare the growth media and plates for the spot assay.

substeps.instruction: Store soft LB agar (0.7% agar) at 50 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Phage Dilutions
steps.instruction: Create a wide range of phage dilutions in LB medium using a 96-well plate.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a dilution range from 10^-1 to 10^-12 to cover possible titers.

steps.title: Prepare and Pour Top Agar
steps.instruction: Mix the bacterial culture with soft agar and apply to plates.

substeps.instruction: Mix 200 µL of cell culture with 3 mL of liquid soft LB agar (50 °C).
Pour the mixture onto the preheated LB agar plates.
Spread the mixture by moving the plate quickly to avoid agar clumps.
Incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Spot Phage Dilutions
steps.instruction: Apply phage dilutions to the prepared plates using a multichannel pipet.

substeps.instruction: Mark the plate beforehand to indicate the dilution range.
Use an 8-channel pipet to gently drop 3 µL of each phage dilution onto the plate (4 rows of 8 drops per plate).
Ensure the pipet does not touch the plate and keep the plate steady to prevent drops from spilling.

steps.title: Dry and Incubate Plates
steps.instruction: Allow the spots to dry and incubate for plaque development.

substeps.instruction: Incubate plates for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Verify that drops have dried; if still visible, incubate longer.
Turn the plates over and incubate overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: Count Plaques and Calculate Titer
steps.instruction: Determine the PFU/mL based on the number of visible plaques.

substeps.instruction: Count the number of plaques (N) for individual drops.
Calculate PFU/mL using the formula: PFU/mL = N × 1/DF × 1/V, where DF is the dilution factor and V is the volume of phage dilution pipetted.
